tex_content.label: D(A)delta(A)
tex_content.html:
For every $A<\infty $ there are $D(A)<\infty $ and $\delta (A)>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $a$, $|\Rm |\leq D(A)$ along every backward flow line from $B(\widetilde x_a,0,A)$ defined for time at most $\delta (A)$. \end{claim}

Proof

\sketch ↗ prop:kappa-limit-noncollapsing ↗ bcbd ↗ controlnbhd The rescaled flows are uniformly noncollapsed and points of scalar curvature above one have doubled canonical neighborhoods. The bounded-curvature-at- bounded-distance estimate bounds scalar curvature on the fixed ball; the canonical-neighborhood evolution inequality then extends this bound for a uniform short backward time. Positive pinching converts the scalar bound to a full curvature bound.

□
